body:
## Problem Statement

A DTCO engineer has a harness that runs a Campaign end to end and nothing worth running in it. The one pack it ships, the opene902 timing probe, was a stand-in for a method: one tool, one report, one chooser that pushes the clock period by the measured slack. Step 3 (D45) ran it for six generations on the reference site and it never converged, because Design Compiler reports a setup slack of exactly zero whenever it meets the period asked, and the chooser loosened the period by its guard band every generation. The owner's ruling was that the fault is the pack's: the first generation's violation already stated the achievable period, and a timing push that knows its business over-constrains and reads the violation. The reference pack carries no such knowledge, and no pack in this product carries any knowledge at all: a pack today is a graph, a contract, a script and two rule files, authored by hand in YAML by the builder.

The product idea promises more than a runner. It promises that a pack author describes the business in plain language, points HimaGuide at a Golden Flow, and is carried through a skill pipeline to a released pack; that a Campaign codes when an exploration node needs a script, a parser or a small tool that does not exist yet; that pack knowledge takes part at planning and judgment moments; and that a Hima tool broken by a site change is repaired on the fly with a record. None of that exists. No code in the harness calls a model. The DeepSeek key the owner holds has never been used by this product. The site's real business, cell-pattern mining feeding an Fmax push on AES on TSMC28, has never run in this harness, and the legacy runs that did it never demonstrated a converging multi-generation loop either.

Step 4 is where the toy stops. The pack is the open question, and the pack is authored by the harness, with the tools and knowledge it needs, and run as a real Campaign with real jobs, in-situ code, the owner's DeepSeek key, and the desktop window.

## Solution

**The author's view.** The pack author opens the HimaHarness window, and in its chat invokes the pack authoring pipeline: five skills, one per stage. The grill stage interviews the author about the business until the intent is unambiguous and writes the pack intent record. The spec stage turns the intent and the Golden Flow into one human-readable pack spec: the Goal template and its constraints, the run contract, the semantics the readers produce, the judge rules, the choosers with the knowledge behind them, the declared endings, the workshops where the AI may write code, and the knowledge files. The fabric stage compiles the spec into the graph and the contract, flags every tool the pack needs and does not have, and writes the ones it can, with the author reviewing each. The test stage runs the pack on the real Site against its Golden Flow and writes the test record, including every self-repair the bring-up needed. The release stage versions the pack with its check results. A pack remains a folder of plain files the author can read, and its stage is what those files say.

**The engineer's view.** The DTCO engineer picks the released pack in the window's start form, confirms the Goal, the inputs and the Budget, and starts the Campaign. The Campaign runs on the Site for hours. When the graph reaches the mining node, the AI writes the cell-need miner for this design and this library in the node's workshop, the fabric ships it into the Campaign workspace and runs it as a Job under the Permit, and a reader turns its output into typed candidates on the ledger. The Fmax probe drills down: it over-constrains the period, reads the violation, computes the achievable period, and converges when successive readings agree. The outer Loop explores mining profiles from the list the pack declared, its chooser picking the next by failure class over the ledger's numbers. Every verdict is a deterministic rule. The Campaign ends the Goal met, converged, or at an ending the pack declared in its own words, such as zero adoption with the library verified, and never at a generation limit it cannot explain. The technical report beside the results says what code was written, what knowledge was cited, and why each Strategy was chosen.

**The harness's view.** One model moment enters the fabric: the workshop. It is an isolated model session with its own instructions, the pack's knowledge at hand, and three tools that go through HimaShell: write into the declared workshop directory, read the declared inputs, read the named knowledge files. The model never has a shell on a Site. What crosses from the session into the fact chain is recorded: the session with its model, and every file written with its hash. The key comes from the owner's environment or the host's own credential store, never from a file the harness writes. Everything else the pack needs, it declares: its Strategy, its readers and their semantics, its rules, its choosers, its knowledge, its endings.

## Boundary and priority: pack first

Step 3 left specifics of the toy inside the harness: the Strategy is one period knob the harness owns, and the readers, rules and choosers ship inside the bundle, so a pack cannot bring its own. HimaPack and HimaHarness together decide whether a Campaign succeeds, and the relationship is collaborative, but the priority is fixed: **changes go into the pack first, and the harness changes only for a gap no pack can fill.** Step 4's harness work is therefore mostly un-specializing: taking the toy's specifics out of the harness so the pack can own them.

Two rules bind every ticket cut from this spec.

1. **The order of repair.** When the Golden Flow fails in this harness, the first fix is the pack: its graph, contract, tools, readers, rules, choosers, knowledge and words, which is where the pipeline's stages and the author work. The second is the pack's tools written or replaced through the workshop at run time, or by the fabric and test stages at authoring time. The harness comes third, only when a test record or an acceptance record shows that no pack can state what is needed, and then as a generic element, recorded as a product decision that names the evidence.
2. **What a harness change may be.** It removes a specific assumption or adds a generic element the pack declares, and it never carries a design, a tool, a report format or a flow's name. Everything that names AES, TSMC28, Design Compiler, Library Compiler, Innovus, bool2cmos, celluzi, a report path or a mining route lives in the pack folder. A script enforces it: the harness's source contains none of the pack's nouns.

The harness elements step 4 builds are listed below with the gap each fills. Everything else the first draft proposed is deferred to the evidence rule and listed as deferred, so that a later reader knows it was set aside on purpose and not forgotten.

## User Stories

**Authoring**

1. As a pack author, I want to describe my business in plain language in the window's chat and be grilled until every ambiguity is resolved, so that the pack encodes my method and not the model's guess.
2. As a pack author, I want the grill to point at the Golden Flow where it lies and raise every place my words and the flow disagree, so that neither side wins silently.
3. As a pack author, I want the grill to end in a pack intent record I can read, so that the answers and the resolved ambiguities are kept with the pack.
4. As a pack author, I want the spec stage to write one pack spec file holding the Goal template, constraints, run contract, semantics, judge rules, choosers, endings, workshops and knowledge references, so that the whole method is in one place a person can review.
5. As a pack author, I want the fabric stage to compile the spec into the graph and the contract and refuse a spec that does not compile, naming the line, so that a pack never reaches a Site with a contradiction in it.
6. As a pack author, I want every tool the pack needs and does not have flagged, and the ones the AI can write written for my review, so that the pack is complete before it is tested.
7. As a pack author, I want the test stage to run the pack on the real Site against the Golden Flow and write a test record, so that a pack without a real run cannot be released.
8. As a pack author, I want every self-repair the test run needed recorded in the test record with the before and after hashes, so that I can fold the repair into the pack rather than leave it as a runtime patch.
9. As a pack author, I want the release stage to version the pack with its check results and make the released folder immutable, so that a Campaign always names a pack that cannot have changed under it.
10. As a pack author, I want the pipeline's own knowledge about what a good pack is, such as over-constrain and read the violation, end honestly in more than one way, and assert the checker options, to be applied and cited during authoring, so that the pack carries knowledge from the first draft.
11. As a pack author, I want the pack's knowledge folder to hold plain Markdown files, so that I can write, read and correct what the model will be given.
12. As a pack author, I want to see the stage a pack is at and its files on the workbench page, so that I know where the pipeline stands without reading the folder.
13. As a pack author, I want to re-enter any stage after a change, so that a correction to the spec recompiles and retests without starting over.
14. As the builder and first author, I want the AES on TSMC28 cell-mining and Fmax-push pack to be the first pack the pipeline produces, so that the pipeline is proven on the business the product is for.

**Running**

15. As a DTCO engineer, I want to pick a released pack in the start form and see its Goal parameters and Strategy knobs in the pack's own words, so that I confirm the business and not a field name.
16. As a DTCO engineer, I want the mining node to write its miner for my design and library at run time, so that the pack does not have to anticipate every netlist and library.
17. As a DTCO engineer, I want every script the AI writes recorded on the ledger with its path and hash, and shown on the card, so that I can read the code that produced a number.
18. As a DTCO engineer, I want the Fmax probe to over-constrain, read the violation, state the achievable period, and converge when successive readings agree, so that the Campaign learns the achievable frequency instead of drifting.
19. As a DTCO engineer, I want the outer Loop to explore mining strategies inside the space the pack declared, so that the AI chooses inside the method and not outside it. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
20. As a DTCO engineer, I want every model-proposed Strategy recorded with the reasons the model gave and the ledger records and knowledge it cited, so that a choice can be audited. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
21. As a DTCO engineer, I want a model proposal outside the declared space refused and recorded, so that no run drifts past its method. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
22. As a DTCO engineer, I want the six mining routes to run in parallel as light Jobs while the Site's one-large-job rule holds for Design Compiler and Innovus, so that free work is not serialised behind licensed work. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
23. As a DTCO engineer, I want the Library Compiler hard gate as a judge whose failure ends the Campaign with the log tail, so that a library the tool refused is never used.
24. As a DTCO engineer, I want the Campaign to end at zero adoption, with the library verified and both halves of the liveness assertion on the ledger, as a declared ending and not a failure, so that a result with no path is still a result.
25. As a DTCO engineer, I want the Goal judged on matched reports of the same tool in both arms, with adoption and verification failures as constraints, so that a five percent claim cannot come from mismatched reports.
26. As a DTCO engineer, I want the judge's qualitative findings, such as why adoption rose while the critical path stayed flat, added beside the verdicts and citing the records they read, so that the report explains and never overrides. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
27. As a DTCO engineer, I want a Hima reader that breaks on the 2025 tools repaired on the fly inside its allowance, with the patch recorded, so that a report-format change does not end my Campaign. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
28. As a DTCO engineer, I want a repair that fails within its allowance to become a Hard blocker I can clear from the window, so that the Campaign waits for me instead of guessing. Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
29. As a DTCO engineer, I want the Campaign to survive a host restart in the middle of a model moment, so that the moment is re-run and the records stay consistent.
30. As a DTCO engineer, I want the technical report to hold the code written, the knowledge cited, the repairs made and the reasons for each Strategy, so that a colleague can read the whole chain.
31. As a DTCO engineer, I want the card to show which model moment a node is in and which session it is, so that a long silence is explained.
32. As a DTCO engineer, I want the Budget's time box to fit a Campaign of hours and the meters to show the time each generation and each Job took, so that I can plan the next one.

**The Site and the owner**

33. As a CAD owner, I want the Permit to stay the one statement of what the harness may touch, with the workshop's directory inside the Campaign workspace and no new write root, so that in-situ code cannot reach the flow, the PDK or the results.
34. As a CAD owner, I want the model to have no shell on my Site, only Hima's tools through HimaShell, so that a model turn cannot run a command the Permit did not decide on.
35. As a CAD owner, I want bool2cmos, celluzi and the Python the miner runs on to be tools my Site provides and the contract names, so that the pack ships none of their code.
36. As a CAD owner, I want every Job's peak memory recorded when the Site can report it, so that the parallel job cap can be raised on evidence (D33). Deferred: built only on the evidence the boundary requires.
37. As the owner, I want the DeepSeek key to come from my launch environment or the host's own credential store, and a test that proves the harness never writes one, so that the product's word on credentials holds.
38. As the owner, I want the model to be deepseek-v4-flash through the DeepSeek API (D9), with the model named on every model-moment record, so that a result can be attributed to the model that produced it.
39. As the owner, I want the reference Site's bring-up of AES on TSMC28 on the 2025 tools to be the pack's test stage and not a hand edit of the site, so that a customer's CAD can repeat it from the contract.

**Proof**

40. As the R&D lead, I want the step-4 acceptance to be one Campaign on the reference site, started from the window with the real key, that wrote its own miner, converged its Fmax probe in both arms, ended at a declared ending, and left the report beside the results, so that the product's claim is observed and not asserted.
41. As the second person (D10), I want to run the released pack end to end from the window without the builder's help, so that the three-month cut's proof is somebody else's.
42. As the R&D lead, I want the acceptance record to say what was skipped or failed in the same words as its passes, so that a partial result is never dressed as a full one.

**The developer**

43. As the harness developer, I want the contract suite to run the model moments and the pipeline without a key, replaying turns a real model produced, so that the suite is deterministic and free.
44. As the harness developer, I want a live check with the real key before any merge that touches a model moment, its record committed, so that the replay never drifts from the host.
45. As the harness developer, I want the stand-in Site to answer every tool the AES pack names with results computed from the Strategy, so that a Campaign of the real graph runs locally in seconds.
46. As the harness developer, I want the stand-in flow to report slack the way Design Compiler does (#54), so that a chooser is proven against the tool's behaviour before it touches the Site.
47. As the harness developer, I want every new dsh seam the model moments use measured on a booted host before it is designed to, so that the reforge's failure is not repeated.

## Implementation Decisions

**In the pack, with no harness change beyond loading the folder:**

- **The Fmax probe** is a drill-down Loop on the act node that synthesizes at the Strategy's period. Its rule chooser over-constrains and reads the violation: on a violation the next period is the asked period plus the violation less a step; on a met period, which Design Compiler reports as zero slack, the next is the asked period less a step; the Loop converges when successive asked periods agree within the band. All of it is D38's clause language over the reads period and slack with one bound step, and the existing convergence on period. No widening of the chooser language is needed.
- **The outer Loop's Strategy** is the mining profile, a choice knob from a declared list, chosen by a rule chooser by failure class as the legacy did: zero adoption jumps to the mapper-fit profile, anything else advances one; convergence is the measured critical path within a band.
- **The contract** names the tools: foundry-only synthesis, mining per route, bool2cmos, celluzi, Liberty characterisation, Library Compiler, synthesis with the generated library, both post-route arms, the verification session; their argv under the Site's wrappers, their licences, the inputs the Site binds, the workspace copy list, the words for every Goal parameter and knob.
- **The readers** are scripts in the pack's tools folder, the semantics they produce declared in the pack's semantics file: the candidate set, the Library Compiler result, adoption through the instance-to-master relation, the matched post-route summaries, the verification counts.
- **The rules** are data in the pack: improvement at least five percent, adopted instances at least one, distinct masters at least one, verification failures zero, Library Compiler errors zero, and the liveness pair the zero-adoption ending requires.
- **The endings** are the pack's words on a judge outcome with no outgoing edge, which already ends a Run: zero adoption with the library verified ends the Run goal-not-met with the pack's sentence on the run row and in the report.
- **The knowledge folder** holds plain Markdown: the verification-gate discipline, the pressure windows, the zero-adoption terminal, the six mining routes and the merge rule, the over-constraining push and why a loosening one drifts.
- **The workshop declaration** on the mining node: purpose, the directory under the Campaign workspace, the wrapper, the inputs it may read, the semantics it must produce.
- **The pack intent record, the pack spec, the version file and the test record** are written by the pipeline's stages into the folder; the stage a pack is at is which of them exist and validate.
- **The bring-up on the 2025 tools** is the pack's test stage; every tool fix is folded into the pack, never into the harness.

**In the harness, each with the gap it fills:**

- **Pack-local data.** The loader resolves rules, choosers, readers and knowledge in the pack folder first and in the bundle second. Gap: a pack cannot ship a chooser, a rule or a reader today; all three live in the bundle. Un-specializing.
- **The Strategy is the pack's.** The contract declares the knobs, each typed as a number with a unit and bounds or a choice from a declared list; the harness stops owning a single period knob; the run row carries the pack's Strategy; node arguments, choosers, convergence and the words block reference knobs by name; the first Strategy on the start form is built from the knobs' declared defaults. Gap: no second knob is possible. Un-specializing; one domain bump; #46 folds in.
- **Readers validated against declared semantics.** A pack reader's output is validated against the semantics file before it becomes an observation; the bundle's existing readers stay and are declared the same way. Gap: a reader today is harness code with a fixed output type. Un-specializing.
- **The workshop moment.** One isolated model session, opened by the fabric through one Hima interface over the agent seam, which moved between dsh versions and is wrapped per ADR-0001 with a booted-host contract test, composed from a Hima agent preset whose tools are exactly three: write a file into the declared workshop directory through HimaShell, read the declared inputs, read the named knowledge files. The harness appends a session record when the moment opens and closes, with the preset, the session id, the model, the node, the generation and the attempt, and a code record for every write, with the path, sha256, bytes, language, node, generation, attempt and session; a write anywhere else is refused in HimaShell's words; the output runs as a Job like any other and is read by the declared reader; a failing script counts against the Retry allowance. The model has no shell and no filesystem on a Site. Gap: nothing in the harness lets a model write code, and that is the owner's requirement. Generic: the harness knows nothing of what is written.
- **The pipeline's skills.** The bundle registers five skills through dsh's programmatic skill provider, a seam unchanged across the tracked versions, user-invocable from the window's chat as grill, spec, fabric, test and release, with the pipeline's own knowledge about packs as reference files beside them. The skills instruct the model to write the pack's files and to use the verbs that exist: pack check, run and status; the test stage starts a Campaign with `/hima run` and writes the test record from its report and records; the release stage writes the version file with the hashes of every file, and pack check refuses a released pack whose files no longer hash to it. The authoring session is the dsh chat of the hima profile with the pack folder as its workspace, so the host's own file tools under its workspace-write sandbox write only there; the Golden Flow is read where it lies. Gap: the pipeline is the product's differentiator and has no home in a pack. Generic.
- **Test stand-ins.** The driver's home seeding gains dsh's keyless replay adapter in place of the DeepSeek adapter in the test profile overlay, fed session fixtures recorded from real sessions with the real key; the stand-in flow answers every tool the pack's contract names with results computed from the Strategy and the arm, slack zero when met and the shortfall when not (#54 first); a live check with the real key, in D24's shape, runs before any merge that touches the workshop or a skill and its record is committed. Gap: the suite cannot run a model. Test infrastructure; the replay package is support tier and pinned exactly.
- **Evidence in the window and the report.** The card shows the workshop state on the node, the code records with a drawer to read the file, the Strategy in the pack's words, the ending's sentence; the report gains sections for code written and knowledge cited; the JSON schema version moves. Gap: evidence not shown is not evidence.
- **The credential path is dsh's, and a test proves it.** The shell passes the launch environment through as today; dsh resolves the key from that environment, from its own credentials file written by the Models page the hima profile carries, or from an env file; the model is deepseek-v4-flash (D9), named on every session record; a contract test proves no file under the home the harness wrote contains a key.
- **Records and the ledger.** New record types session and code; the run row carries the pack's Strategy and the ending's words. One domain bump per merged slice with its reason in the bump log.
- **Documents.** CONTEXT.md gains Workshop, Model moment and Knowledge file when each is settled by its ticket. Product decisions record the pack-first boundary and its order of repair, the Strategy as the pack's, the workshop's bounds, the pipeline as skills with stage as files, and the replay in the suite with the live check before merge. The product idea's out-of-scope list is corrected where step 4 lands what it deferred.

**Deferred until a test record or an acceptance record shows a pack cannot state it:**

- A model chooser and a planner moment: the first pack chooses its next profile by a rule.
- Judge findings and a judge moment: the verdicts and the report's reasoning stand without them.
- Runtime self-repair as its own moment: a failing pack tool is replaced through a workshop declaration at run time or fixed at authoring time in the test stage; the harness's own readers stay as they are unless a record shows one broke.
- Light and heavy Job classes and peak-memory recording: the mining routes fork and serialise on the reference Site's cap of one (D33).
- Derived values in the chooser language.
- A declared-endings schema beyond the pack's words on an ending.
- A packs band on the workbench page: the chat shows the pipeline.
- A compile verb: the fabric stage's skill writes the graph and the contract, and pack check validates them.

## Testing Decisions

- **A good test drives the product the engineer or the author uses and asserts on what they would see or read.** For step 4 that is the desktop shell in driver mode: invoke a pipeline skill in the window's chat and read the pack folder and the packs band; start a Campaign of the AES pack's graph from the form; watch the card show a model moment, a code record, a planner decision, a finding, a repair, a declared ending; read the ledger and the report through the routes with the session the shell established. No test asserts on a module's internals, no test opens a session by a path the shell does not use, no test carries a key.
- **The one seam stays the desktop shell in driver mode**, containing the booted host one level up as step 3 left it. Two stand-ins sit beside it: the local Site with the stand-in flow, and the keyless replay adapter with recorded fixtures. Step-1 to step-3 tests are left as they are. The in-process boot stays for a chat command's words only.
- **What is tested through it:** each pipeline stage producing its artifact and refusing what it must; the AES pack's compiled graph loading and checking against the local Site with its pack-local rules, choosers and readers; a reader's output refused when it does not match the semantics file; the workshop writing inside its directory and refused outside it, the code record's hash matching the file, the script running as a Job and its output read as declared semantics; the six routes forking and serialising under the cap; the library gate ending the Run with the tail; the zero-adoption ending in the pack's words; the Fmax probe converging on the honest stand-in and a loosening chooser diverging on it, so the difference is a test; the pack's Strategy on the form, the card and the report in the pack's words; restart in the middle of the workshop moment; the home holding no key; the fence on every new route; the boundary script finding none of the pack's nouns in the harness.
- **Prior art:** the window and fabric suites and the driver support of step 3; the pack suite for loading and checking; the step-3 acceptance script for a record whose every claim is a check; the research note's per-seam contract tests for the skills row and the agent seam.
- **The acceptance** for step 4 is a script in the shape of step 3's, on the reference site, with the real key, started from the window: the released AES pack authored through the pipeline with its test record; a Campaign in which the miner was written in the workshop and ran; the Fmax probe converged in the foundry-only arm and the generated arm; the library gate passed or ended the Run as declared; the Campaign ended goal met, converged, or at an ending the pack declared in its words, never on the generation limit; the report on the site with the new sections; the restart read-back; every command audited; nothing written outside the workspace. The step-4 done entry cites it, and the second person's run (D10) is recorded beside it as the ladder's proof.

## Out of Scope

A pack source or marketplace beyond a local release folder; a second Site or multi-site binding; a second pack beyond the AES on TSMC28 cell-mining and Fmax-push pack; multi-user authorisation; packaging and signing the desktop app; risk mode in its broad sense (repairing Site infrastructure or pack delivery); a local model (D9); token or money budgets (D4); a general expression language for choosers beyond derived values; a knowledge index or search engine; nesting drill-down deeper than one level; the SKY130 and Cool3D legacy packs; GUI EDA tools; a model that writes verdicts or changes a Goal; changing the step-1 to step-3 tests' seams; any harness change that carries a design, tool, report format or flow name, or that a pack could state instead.

## Further Notes

**The order in which step 4 is observed on the real server**, each a customer-visible behaviour and the shape the tickets follow:

1. **The probe.** The pipeline authors the Fmax probe Loop of the AES pack from the Golden Flow, grill to release, and the probe converges on AES on TSMC28 on the 2025 tools with the over-constraining chooser, the bring-up's repairs in the test record. This is the first converging Loop on the site.
2. **The workshop.** The mining node's miner is written at run time, forked over the six routes and serialised on the Site's cap, its candidates read as typed semantics, judged; the cells built through bool2cmos and celluzi; the library gate.
3. **The Campaign.** Both arms probed and measured on matched post-route reports, the rule chooser picking the next profile by failure class, an honest ending in the pack's words, the report with its new sections.
4. **The proof.** The second person runs the released pack from the window.

**Prefactors and folded tickets.** #54 (the honest stand-in) comes first. #39 (a contract names the clock group), #46 (Strategy in the pack's words) and #48 (the band overridable at start) fold into the Strategy and chooser work. The refactor tickets #32, #33, #49, #50, #51, #53 are taken as prefactors where a step-4 slice touches their module; #34, #35, #36, #37, #38, #40, #44, #45, #47, #52 stay open as hygiene.

**Risks named, not dissolved.** AES on TSMC28 is not a Design Zoo combination on the reference site: the pack brings its own flow and bindings as the legacy Campaigns did, and the 28 nm bring-up on the Synopsys 2025.06 and Cadence 23.14 releases is real work that self-repair is meant to absorb but may not; a read-only probe of what the legacy flow left on the site, including bool2cmos and celluzi, precedes any design. The legacy's Fmax gate read matched Innovus post-route reports; Innovus is uncounted node-locked on the site and its Jobs are long, so a Campaign is hours and the acceptance's Budget is the owner's call. The dsh agent seam moved at the tracked version and is wrapped, not used directly. The replay package is support tier. The archive's "603 runs" figure in the product idea cannot be re-derived from the archive and is left as unverified. The model may not carry the reasoning the workshop needs; a miner it cannot write within the Retry allowance is a Hard blocker the author clears by writing the tool into the pack, and the effect of knowledge is measured in the test record, never promised.

**Terms.** Workshop: the scope on an act node where the AI writes and runs code, a directory under the Campaign workspace, a wrapper, and a declared output. Model moment: a point in a Run where an isolated model session takes part; the workshop is the one step 4 builds. Knowledge file: a plain Markdown file in a pack's knowledge folder, cited by path and heading.
title: Step 4: the pack — HimaGuide authors the AES on TSMC28 cell-mining and Fmax-push HimaPack with the tools and knowledge it needs, and HimaFabric runs it as a real Campaign with in-situ code, on the owner's DeepSeek key, from the desktop window
